slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Not covered here? Ask us directly — same working day response.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: We act as your IT department for a fixed monthly fee. That covers an unlimited service desk, proactive monitoring, patching, endpoint security and onsite visits when something needs hands on it. The point is that most problems get caught or fixed before they interrupt anyone.

slots.label: Question 2
slots.default: How is it different from break-fix?

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Break-fix pays someone to turn up after it has already gone wrong, which means your costs are unpredictable and your provider only earns when you have problems. Managed support inverts that. We are paid the same whether your month is quiet or chaotic, so we have every reason to make it quiet.

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Unlimited support requests. Ask as often as you need, with no per-ticket charging. Project work is scoped separately, because migrations, office moves and large rollouts are a different kind of job. Hardware and licences are yours, though we procure and manage them for you.

slots.label: Question 4
slots.default: Is it suitable for smaller teams?

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: Yes, and small teams often feel the benefit fastest, because there is nobody internally who can absorb an IT problem. The scope is matched to your size, so you are not paying for enterprise processes you will never use.

slots.label: Question 5
slots.default: Can you work alongside our existing IT person?

slots.label: Paragraph 6
slots.default: Often that is the best arrangement. We take the day-to-day tickets, monitoring and patching so they can concentrate on the things only they can do, or we sit behind them as escalation and holiday cover. Either way they stop being the single point of failure.

slots.label: Paragraph 7
slots.default: We assess what you have and what the business actually needs, agree a support plan, deploy the tooling we use for remote support, monitoring and patching, then go live. You get a named point of contact rather than a ticket portal and a shrug.
